find: On the upper chest near the shoulder, about one thumb-width below the soft hollow under the outer collarbone, level with the gap just below the first rib (about six thumb-widths out from the middle of the chest).
On the upper chest, in the soft hollow just under the outer end of the collarbone, on the chest side of the bony knob at the front of the shoulder.
On the inner upper arm along the thumb side of the biceps muscle, about four finger-widths below the armpit fold.
On the inner upper arm along the thumb side of the biceps muscle, about four finger-widths plus one thumb-width below the front armpit fold.
In the elbow crease with the arm bent, in the dip on the thumb side of the thick tendon in the middle of the crease.
On the thumb side of the inner forearm, on the line from wrist to elbow, one thumb-width above the halfway point between the wrist crease and the elbow crease.
On the thumb side of the forearm, about two finger-widths above the wrist crease, in the groove next to the bony bump at the wrist.
On the thumb side of the inner forearm, one thumb-width above the wrist crease, between the wrist bone bump and the pulse.
At the wrist crease on the thumb side, in the soft dip just beside where you feel the pulse. Press next to the pulse, not on it.
On the palm, along the edge of the thumb's fleshy pad, halfway down the long thumb-side hand bone where the darker skin meets the paler palm skin.
On the outer edge of the thumb, just beside the base corner of the thumbnail, on the side away from the index finger.
On the index finger, on the side nearest the thumb, just beside the base corner of the fingernail.
On the thumb side of the index finger, in the small dip just past the big knuckle toward the fingertip, where the darker skin meets the paler skin.
On the back of the hand, in the hollow on the thumb side of the index finger's big knuckle, just on the wrist side of it.
On the back of the hand, on the thumb side of the index-finger hand bone, about halfway along it, in the fleshy web between thumb and index finger.
On the back of the wrist at the thumb side, in the little hollow that appears between the two thumb tendons when you lift your thumb up.
On the thumb-side back of the forearm, about four finger-widths above the wrist crease, on the line toward the outer elbow.
On the thumb-side back of the forearm, on the line toward the outer elbow, a little under halfway from the wrist crease to the elbow crease (about five thumb-widths up).
On the thumb-side back of the forearm, on the line to the wrist, about four finger-widths plus one thumb-width below the outer end of the elbow crease.
On the thumb-side back of the forearm, about four finger-widths below the outer end of the elbow crease, on the line to the wrist.
On the thumb-side back of the forearm, about three finger-widths below the outer end of the elbow crease, in the thick muscle.
With the elbow bent, at the outer end of the elbow crease, in the dip on the thumb side just before the bony knob.
On the outer elbow, about one thumb-width above the bony knob on the outside of the elbow, at the front edge of the ridge there.
On the outer upper arm, about four finger-widths above the outer end of the elbow crease, on the line up to the shoulder.
On the outer upper arm, about three-quarters of the way up from the elbow crease to the armpit, just in front of the lower tip of the rounded shoulder muscle.
On the outer front of the shoulder, in the hollow just in front of and below the bony tip of the shoulder, easiest to feel when you lift your arm out to the side.
On the top of the shoulder, in the groove between the outer end of the collarbone and the ridge of the shoulder blade, near the shoulder tip.
On the side of the neck, about one thumb-width below the level of the Adam's apple, just behind the back edge of the thick neck muscle. Light touch only.
On the side of the neck, level with the Adam's apple, in the gap between the two parts of the thick neck muscle. Light touch only, beside the pulse.
On the upper lip area, directly below the outer edge of the nostril, level with the middle of the groove under the nose.
On the face in the groove beside the nostril, level with the middle of the outer edge of the nostril wing.
On the face, straight below the pupil when looking ahead, right on the edge of the lower eye socket, at the point where the eyeball sits just above.
avoidReason: Sits between the eyeball and the lower eye-socket rim; pressing here pushes into the eye.

find: On the face, about a thumb-width straight below the pupil when looking ahead, in the small dip in the cheekbone just under the eye socket.
On the face, straight below the pupil when looking ahead, level with the bottom of the nostril wing, just outside the crease running from nose to mouth.
On the face, just beside the corner of the mouth, about half a finger-width out, on the line of the crease that runs down from the nose.
On the jaw, just in front of the angle of the jawbone, in the dip at the front edge of the chewing muscle. You may feel a pulse there; press beside it, lightly.
On the jaw, about one finger-width in front of and above the angle of the jawbone, where the chewing muscle bulges when you clench your teeth.
On the side of the face, about a finger-width in front of the ear, in the hollow just under the cheekbone arch. With your mouth closed you feel a dip; it fills when you open your mouth.
At the corner of the forehead on each side, about half a thumb-width inside the hairline, where the hairline turns back toward the temple.
On the front of the neck beside the Adam's apple, just in front of the large neck muscle, right where you feel the pulse of the carotid artery.
avoidReason: Lies directly over the common carotid artery; pressing here is unsafe.

find: On the front of the neck, along the front edge of the large neck muscle, a little below the level of the Adam's apple, about halfway between the carotid pulse and the inner end of the collarbone.
At the base of the front of the neck, in the small dip just above the inner end of the collarbone, between the two tendons of the neck muscle.
In the hollow just above the middle of the collarbone, in line with the nipple, in the dip at the base of the side of the neck.
On the upper chest, just below the middle of the collarbone, four thumb-widths out from the breastbone midline, straight above the nipple.
On the upper chest, in the gap between the first and second ribs, four thumb-widths out from the breastbone midline, straight above the nipple.
On the chest, in the gap just below the second rib, four thumb-widths out from the breastbone midline, straight above the nipple. The second rib joins the breastbone at its raised ridge.
On the chest, in the gap between the third and fourth ribs, four thumb-widths out from the breastbone midline, just above the nipple.
At the centre of the nipple. It is used only as a measuring landmark for the chest and abdomen, not as a treatment point.
avoidReason: On the nipple; used only as a landmark, not for self-pressing.

find: On the chest, directly below the nipple in the gap between the fifth and sixth ribs. In women it is at the crease under the breast.
On the upper belly, on both sides, just under the rib edge, about two hand-widths above the navel and about three finger-widths out from the midline.
On the upper belly, five thumb-widths above the navel and two thumb-widths out from the midline, about one thumb-width below the lower edge of the ribs.
On the upper belly, four thumb-widths above the belly button and two thumb-widths out from the midline.
On the upper belly, three thumb-widths above the belly button and two thumb-widths out from the midline.
On the upper belly, two thumb-widths above the navel and two thumb-widths out to the side of the midline.

In the crease where the lower belly meets the thigh, level with the top of the pubic bone and two thumb-widths out from the midline. Feel for the pulse and press beside it.
On the upper front of the thigh, straight below the bony point at the front of the hip, level with the bottom of the pubic bone, in the soft dip between the thigh muscles.
On the front-outer thigh, about six thumb-widths above the top of the kneecap, on the line toward the hip bone's front point.
On the front-outer thigh, about three thumb-widths above the top of the kneecap, just outside the large thigh tendon.
On the front-outer thigh, about two thumb-widths above the top of the kneecap, in the groove between the thigh tendon and the outer thigh muscle.
With the knee bent, in the hollow just below the kneecap on its outer side, beside the thick tendon under the kneecap.
On the front of the lower leg, about four finger-widths below the kneecap's lower edge and one finger-width outside the shin bone, in the muscle.
On the front of the lower leg, about six thumb-widths below the knee hollow and one finger-width outside the shin bone, in the muscle.
On the front of the lower leg, about eight thumb-widths below the knee hollow, one finger-width outside the shin bone, roughly midway to the ankle.
On the front of the lower leg, about nine thumb-widths below the knee hollow and one finger-width outside the shin bone, a little below the midpoint.
On the front-outer lower leg, halfway between the knee and the ankle bone, about two finger-widths outside the sharp edge of the shin bone, in the muscle.
On the front of the ankle, in the middle of the crease where foot meets leg, in the hollow between the two big tendons. They stand out when you lift your toes.
On the top of the foot, at the highest part of the arch, where you can feel a pulse. Press gently beside the pulse, not on it.
On the top of the foot, in the groove between the bones leading to the second and third toes, in the hollow just behind the toe knuckle.
On the top of the foot, just behind the web between the second and third toes, in the small dip beside the base of the second toe.
On the second toe, at the outer corner of the nail, right where the side edge meets the base of the nail.
On the inner side of the big toe, right at the corner of the nail, just behind the nail's base.
On the inner side of the big toe, just in front of the big knuckle joint, where the skin changes from the top of the foot to the sole.
On the inner edge of the foot, in the hollow just behind the big knuckle joint, where the skin changes from top-of-foot to sole.
On the inner edge of the foot, in the hollow just in front of and below the bump at the base of the big toe's long bone, where the skin changes color.
On the inside of the ankle, in the soft hollow just in front of and below the inner ankle bone, halfway between that bone and the bump in front of it.
On the inside of the lower leg, about four finger-widths above the tip of the inner ankle bone, just behind the edge of the shin bone.
On the inside of the lower leg, about eight finger-widths above the inner ankle bone (twice as high as the point four finger-widths up), just behind the edge of the shin bone.
On the inside of the lower leg, about four finger-widths below the hollow under the knee's bony bump, just behind the edge of the shin bone.
On the inside of the leg just below the knee, in the hollow where the shin bone's edge meets the underside of the bony bump below the inner knee.

On the inner thigh, about a third of the way down from the groin crease to the knee, in the groove between the front and inner thigh muscles where a pulse can be felt. Press beside the pulse, not on it.
In the fold where the thigh meets the lower belly, a little outside the pulse you can feel in the groin, level with the top of the pubic bone.
On the lower belly, four thumb-widths (a hand-width plus a thumb-width) out from the midline, a little above the crease where the thigh meets the pelvis.

On the side of the upper chest, in the soft gap between the third and fourth ribs, well outside the breastbone.
On the upper chest, in the soft gap between the second and third ribs, well out to the side of the breastbone, below the collarbone.
On the side of the chest, in the soft gap between the sixth and seventh ribs, straight down from the middle of the armpit.
In the center of the armpit hollow, directly over the artery and nerves.

find: On the inner side of the upper arm, just along the inner edge of the biceps muscle, about four finger-widths above the elbow crease.

On the palm side of the forearm, half a thumb-width above the wrist crease, on the thumb side of the tendon on the little-finger edge.
On the palm side of the wrist, in the small hollow on the little-finger side of the crease, just beside the tendon and the small bone there.
On the palm, between the bones of the ring and little fingers, just behind the knuckles, where the little fingertip lands when you make a fist.

At the back of the shoulder, above the back armpit fold, in the dip just under the ridge of the shoulder blade.
On the shoulder blade, in the dip in the middle of the flat area below the ridge, about a third of the way down from the ridge toward the bottom tip of the blade.
On the top of the shoulder blade, in the hollow above the middle of its ridge, in the muscle you can squeeze at the top of the shoulder.

On the top of the shoulder blade, in the hollow just above the inner end of its ridge, about halfway between the back of the shoulder and the spine at the second bump below the big bump at the base of the neck.
On the upper back, beside the spine, about a hand's width (four fingers) out from the first bump below the neck bump, level with the inner edge of the shoulder blade.
On the upper back, about three finger-widths (two thumb-widths) out to the side of the big bump at the base of the neck, level with its lower edge.
On the side of the neck, just behind the big neck muscle running from ear to collarbone, level with the Adam's apple.
On the side of the neck, just behind the angle of the jaw, in the dip right in front of the big neck muscle.
On the face, in the dip along the lower edge of the cheekbone, straight below the outer corner of the eye.
Just in front of the little flap at the ear opening, in the dip that appears when you open your mouth slightly.
On the face, in the small dip just above and inside the inner corner of the eye, against the side of the nose bridge. Use very light pressure and keep the fingertip on the bone, not the eye.
At the inner end of the eyebrow, in the small notch you can feel on the bone, straight above the inner corner of the eye.
On the forehead, straight up from the inner end of the eyebrow, about half a thumb-width inside the hairline.
At the front hairline, about two finger-widths out from the middle of the forehead hairline, half a thumb-width up into the hair.
On the scalp, one thumb-width behind the front hairline and two finger-widths out from the midline.
On the top of the scalp, about two and a half thumb-widths behind the front hairline and two finger-widths out from the midline.
On the top of the head, four thumb-widths behind the front hairline and two finger-widths out from the midline.
On the top of the head, about five and a half thumb-widths behind the front hairline, two finger-widths out from the midline and a little behind the crown.
On the back of the head, about one thumb-width out from the midline, level with the top of the bony bump at the center of the skull base.
On the back of the neck, just below the skull, in the hollow on the outer side of the thick vertical neck muscle, a thumb-width out from the midline.
On the upper back. Find the big bump at the base of the neck, go down one more bump, then two finger-widths out from the spine, level with the lower edge of that second bump.

find: On the upper back, two finger-widths out from the spine, level with the second bump below the big bump at the base of the neck.
On the upper back, about two finger-widths out from the spine, level with the line across the inner ends of the shoulder blade ridges.
Between the shoulder blades, two finger-widths out from the spine, one bump below the level of the inner ends of the shoulder-blade ridges.
Between the shoulder blades, two finger-widths out from the spine, two bumps below the level of the inner ends of the shoulder-blade ridges.

On the mid-back, about two finger-widths out from the spine, level with the bottom tip of the shoulder blade.

On the mid-back, two finger-widths out from the spine, three bumps below the level of the bottom tips of the shoulder blades.
On the mid-back, two finger-widths out from the spine, one bump above the last bone that carries a rib.
On the mid-back, about two finger-widths out from the spine, level with the last rib-bearing bone, about halfway between the shoulder blades and hips.
On the lower back, two finger-widths out from the spine, level with the first bump below the last rib-bearing bone.
On the low back, two finger-widths out from the spine, level with the waist. It sits about halfway between the lowest rib and the top of the hip bone.
On the low back, two finger-widths out from the spine, one bump above the level of the top of the hip bones.
On the low back, two finger-widths out from the spine, at the height of the top of the hip bones, where a belt line would cross.
On the low back, two finger-widths out from the spine, one bump below the level of the top of the hip bones, just above the flat bone at the base of the spine.
On the lower back over the sacrum (the flat bone above the tailbone), two finger-widths out from the midline, a little above the dimple that sits over the buttock.
On the flat bone at the base of the spine (sacrum), two finger-widths out from the midline, level with the dimples above the buttocks.
On the flat bone at the base of the spine (sacrum), two finger-widths out from the midline, about one thumb-width below the level of the dimples above the buttocks.
On the lower back over the sacrum (the flat bone above the tailbone), two finger-widths out from the midline, near the bottom of the sacrum, close to where the buttock crease begins.
On the sacrum, in the small dent just above the buttock dimple, about halfway between the spine line and the bony bump of the hip.
On the sacrum, in the small dent level with the dimple above the buttock, about halfway between that dimple (the bony bump of the hip) and the spine line.
On the sacrum, in the third small dent from the top, about one thumb-width below the level of the dimples, between the midline and the dimple line.
On the lowest part of the sacrum, in the fourth small dent from the top, near the start of the buttock crease, between the midline and the dimple line.
Right beside the very tip of the tailbone, in the soft hollow about half a thumb-width to the side of the buttock cleft.
avoidReason: Lies inside the buttock cleft beside the tip of the tailbone, next to the anal and perineal area; not suitable for self-pressing.

find: At the very middle of the crease where the buttock meets the back of the thigh.

At the outer end of the crease behind the knee, in the dent just inside the tight outer hamstring tendon.
At the center of the crease behind the knee, in the middle of the hollow, with the leg relaxed.

On the upper back, four finger-widths out from the spine, along the inner edge of the shoulder blade, level with the inner ends of the shoulder-blade ridges.

On the back of the calf, in the groove between the two calf-muscle bulges, about three finger-widths below the middle of the back-of-knee crease.
On the back of the calf, in the thickest part of the calf muscle, about halfway between the middle of the back-of-knee crease and the V-shaped notch where the calf muscle ends.

On the outer back of the lower leg, about a thumb-width outward and below the V-notch of the calf muscle, roughly seven thumb-widths above the outer ankle bone.
On the outer back of the lower leg, between the thin outer leg bone and the Achilles tendon, about four finger-widths above the hollow behind the outer ankle bone.
On the outer ankle, in the hollow between the bump of the outer ankle bone and the Achilles tendon.
On the outer side of the heel, straight down from the hollow between the outer ankle bone and the Achilles tendon, on the side of the heel bone where darker and paler skin meet.
On the outer side of the foot, in the hollow just below the bottom edge of the outer ankle bone.
On the outer edge of the foot, in front of and below the outer ankle bone, in the hollow just behind the bump on the little-toe side of the foot.
On the outer edge of the foot, just in front of the bony bump halfway along the foot, where darker skin meets paler skin.
On the outer edge of the foot, in the hollow just behind the knuckle of the little toe, where darker skin meets paler skin.
On the outer edge of the little toe's base, in the hollow just in front of the knuckle, where darker skin meets paler skin.
On the little toe, at the outer side of the nail, a hair's breadth behind the corner of the toenail.

find: Two vertical lines on each side of the lower back: an inner line about two finger-widths from the spine and an outer line about four finger-widths from it, level with the waist.
On the sole, in the dip that appears when you curl your toes, about a third of the way from the base of the toes to the heel.
On the inner edge of the foot, just below the bony bump in the middle of the arch, where the darker top skin meets the paler sole skin.

On the inner lower leg, about two thumb-widths above the inner ankle bone, at the front edge of the Achilles tendon.

On the inner lower calf, about five thumb-widths above the inner ankle bone, in the groove between the bottom of the calf muscle and the Achilles tendon.
On the back of the knee, at the inner end of the crease when the knee is bent, just outside the tendon you can feel on the inner side.
On the lowest part of the belly just above the pubic bone, about half a thumb-width to the side of the midline.
avoidReason: Sits at the top of the pubic bone, in the genital area, where it cannot be pressed comfortably or sensibly on yourself.

On the little-finger side of the ring finger, just behind the corner of the nail, where the side of the nail meets its base.
On the back of the hand, in the small hollow just above the skin fold between the ring finger and little finger.
On the back of the hand, in the groove between the ring- and little-finger bones, just behind the knuckles on the wrist side.
On the back of the wrist, right on the crease, in the dip on the little-finger side of the bundle of finger tendons, in line with the gap between the ring- and little-finger bones.
On the back of the forearm, about three finger-widths above the wrist crease, in the groove between the two forearm bones, directly opposite the popular inner-wrist point.
On the back of the forearm, about four finger-widths above the wrist crease, in the groove between the two forearm bones.
On the back of the forearm, about four finger-widths above the wrist crease, just beside the bone on the little-finger side, about one finger-width over from the middle of the forearm.
On the back of the forearm, in the groove between the two forearm bones, about one-third of the way from the wrist crease to the tip of the elbow.
On the back of the forearm, in the groove between the two forearm bones, five thumb-widths (a hand-width plus three finger-widths) below the tip of the elbow.
On the back of the arm, about one thumb-width above the tip of the elbow, in the hollow you feel when the elbow is bent.
On the back of the upper arm, about three finger-widths above the tip of the elbow, in the middle of the arm.
On the back of the upper arm, in the middle of the arm, five thumb-widths (a hand-width plus three finger-widths) above the tip of the elbow.
On the back of the upper arm, about four finger-widths below the back corner of the shoulder bone, along the rear edge of the rounded shoulder muscle.
On the back of the shoulder, in the dimple just behind and below the bony tip of the shoulder. It shows up when you raise the arm out to the side.
On the upper back, just above the upper inner corner of the shoulder blade, about halfway between the top of the shoulder muscle and the inner end of the shoulder blade's upper edge.
On the side of the neck, just behind the big neck muscle, level with the angle of the jaw.
Just behind the earlobe, in the soft hollow between the jawbone and the bony bump behind the ear.
On the bony bump behind the ear, near its middle, in line with the curve that runs from behind the earlobe up around the ear.
Behind the ear, on the curved line that runs from behind the earlobe up to the tip of the ear, about one-third of the way down from the tip.
On the side of the head just above the tip of the ear. Fold the ear forward, and the spot is where the tip touches the scalp.
In front of the ear, in the small dip just above the little flap at the ear opening. It deepens when you open your mouth slightly.
On the side of the head, just in front of the top of the ear and at the edge of the temple hair. You can feel a pulse right in front of it; stay behind that.
At the outer end of the eyebrow, in the small hollow on the bone.
On the face, in the small hollow on the bony rim just beside the outer corner of the eye, about half a thumb-width out.
Just in front of the small notch at the bottom of the ear's front flap, in the hollow behind the jaw joint; it is easiest to feel with the mouth open.
On the side of the face in front of the ear, in the dip just above the middle of the cheekbone arch.
On the temple inside the hairline, about a quarter of the way down the gentle curve from the forehead corner of the hairline to just above the ear.
On the temple inside the hairline, halfway along the gentle curve from the forehead corner of the hairline to the point just above and in front of the ear.
On the temple inside the hairline, about three-quarters of the way down the gentle curve from the forehead corner toward the front of the ear.
At the temple, where the hairline in front of the ear curves, level with the top of the ear. Press in the small dip there.
On the side of the head, about two finger-widths straight above the tip of the ear. It is easier to feel while you chew.
Above and behind the ear: from the back edge of where the ear joins the head, go straight up about two and a half finger-widths into the hair, a fingertip behind the point above the ear tip.
Behind the ear, roughly level with the top of the ear, about a thumb-width into the hair, on the curve running down toward the bony bump behind the earlobe.
Behind the ear, in the hair just above and behind the bony bump behind the earlobe, about two thirds of the way down the curve from the top of the ear to the hollow below that bump.
Just behind and below the bony bump behind the earlobe, in the soft hollow there.
On the forehead just inside the hairline, a little above the outer end of the eyebrow line, about four finger-widths out from the middle of the forehead.
On the forehead, straight above the pupil when looking ahead, about one thumb-width above the eyebrow.
On the scalp straight above the pupil when looking ahead, about half a thumb-width back from the front edge of the hair.
On the scalp, straight above the pupil, about two finger-widths back from the front hairline.
note: Older references place this a little further back from the hairline. This follows the WHO 2008 measurement.

find: On the scalp straight above the pupil, about two and a half thumb-widths (three to four finger-widths) back from the front hairline.
note: Older references place this a little further back from the hairline. This follows the WHO 2008 measurement.

find: On the scalp, straight above the pupil, about four thumb-widths back from the front hairline.
note: Older references place this a little further back from the hairline. This follows the WHO 2008 measurement.

find: On the back of the head, level with the top of the bony lump in the middle of the skull base, about three finger-widths out to the side, straight above the point in the neck hollow.
At the base of the skull, in the hollow between the two thick neck cords at the back and the muscle that runs up behind the ear, below the ridge of the skull.
On top of the shoulder, halfway between the bump at the base of the neck and the outer tip of the shoulder, on the thick muscle you can squeeze.
On the side of the ribcage with the arm raised, about four finger-widths below the centre of the armpit, in the gap between two ribs.
On the side of the chest, a thumb-width in front of the midline of the armpit, in the groove between the ribs about level with the nipple.
note: WHO places this in the 4th rib gap; some references use the 5th.

find: Straight down from the nipple, count three rib gaps lower (the nipple sits at about the fourth gap; this is the seventh), near the lower edge of the rib cage. In women, go straight down from mid-collarbone.
On the side of the waist, just below the loose tip of the lowest rib, which you can feel behind the lower edge of the rib cage.
On the side of the waist, just below the tip of the second-lowest floating rib, at about belly-button height.
On the side of the lower belly, just inside the front point of the hip bone, level with a spot four finger-widths below the belly button.
On the lower belly, a half thumb-width below and slightly toward the middle from the front point of the hip bone.
On the side of the hip, halfway between the front point of the hip bone and the bony bump on the outer upper thigh.
On the buttock, about one-third of the way from the bony bump on the outer hip toward the dip above the tailbone. Easiest to find lying on your side with the top knee bent.
On the outer thigh, where the tip of your middle finger lands when you stand with your arms hanging straight down.
note: WHO describes this only as where your middle fingertip rests with your arms by your sides. Some references give a fixed seven thumb-widths above the knee crease.

find: On the outer thigh, about seven thumb-widths (a little over two hand-widths) above the outer end of the back-of-knee crease, just behind the thick band along the outer thigh.
note: WHO places this seven thumb-widths above the knee crease; some older references give five.

find: On the outer side of the knee, in the soft dip just above the knob of the thigh bone, between the thick outer band and the hamstring tendon behind it.
On the outer side of the leg, in the soft hollow just in front of and below the knob of bone below the outer knee.
On the outer lower leg, about seven thumb-widths (a little over two hand-widths) above the outer ankle bone, just behind the thin outer shin bone.
On the outer lower leg, about seven thumb-widths (a little over two hand-widths) above the outer ankle bone, on the front edge of the thin outer shin bone.
On the outer lower leg, about five thumb-widths above the ankle bone, on the front edge of the thin outer shin bone.
On the outer lower leg, about four thumb-widths above the ankle bone, just in front of the thin outer shin bone.
On the outer lower leg, about three thumb-widths (four finger-widths) above the outer ankle bone, in the dip on the front edge of the thin outer shin bone.
In front of and below the outer ankle bone, in the hollow on the outer side of the tendon that runs to the little toes (lift the toes to see it).
On top of the foot, in the groove between the bones of the fourth and little toes, just in front of where they meet, on the outer side of the tendon to the little toe.
indications: headache at the side of the head

find: On top of the foot, in the groove between the bones of the fourth and little toes, just behind the knuckle of the fourth toe.
On top of the foot, in the web between the fourth and little toes, a bit toward the ankle from the edge of the skin fold.
On the outer side of the fourth toe, at the corner of the nail, a hair's breadth behind the nail edge.
On the big toe, on the side facing the second toe, at the base corner of the toenail, just a hair back from where the nail meets the skin.
On the top of the foot, in the groove between the big toe and second toe, a little way back from the edge of the web, where the skin colour changes.
On the top of the foot, in the hollow between the big-toe and second-toe bones, just toe-side of where they join; you can feel the foot pulse here.

At the front of the inner ankle, in front of the ankle bump: lift your foot to make the thick tendon at the front of the ankle stand out, then press the soft dip just on the inner (big-toe) side of that tendon.
On the inner shin, in the middle of the flat inner edge of the shinbone, about five thumb-widths above the ankle bone.
On the inner shin, in the middle of the flat inner edge of the shinbone, about seven thumb-widths above the ankle bone.
Just below the bony bump on the inner side of the knee, about one thumb-width behind the soft dip found there, at the top of the calf.
With the knee bent, on the inner side of the knee, in the hollow just in front of the thick tendons at the inner end of the crease behind the knee.
On the inner thigh, about four thumb-widths above the inner edge of the kneecap, in the groove between the two muscles there.
On the inner upper thigh, about three thumb-widths below the groin fold, where you can feel a pulse.
On the inner upper thigh, about two thumb-widths below the groin fold, just outside the thick cord-like muscle of the inner thigh.
In the groin crease, level with the top of the pubic bone and about two and a half thumb-widths out from the midline, where you may feel the groin pulse nearby; press beside the pulse, not on it.
On the side of the belly, just below the tip of the second-lowest floating rib; lying on your side with your top arm raised helps you feel it.

On the chest, straight below the nipple, in the gap between the sixth and seventh ribs, two rib-gaps below nipple level. For women, go straight down from the middle of the collarbone to the same rib gap, under the breast.
Between the tip of the tailbone and the anus, in the perineal area.
avoidReason: Located in the perineal area beside the anus; it cannot be pressed comfortably or hygienically on your own.

find: At the very bottom of the spine, in the small dip just above where the buttock crease begins, on the midline.
On the midline of the lower back, in the dip under the bump of the spine level with the top of your hip bones.
On the midline of the lower back, in the dip under the second lower-back bump, roughly level with the navel on the front.
On the midline of the lower back, in the dip just under the first lower-back spine bump, one bump above the point level with the navel.
On the midline of the back, in the dip under the 11th chest-level spine bump, near the lowest ribs.
On the midline of the back, in the dip under the 10th chest-level spine bump, just above the waist.
On the midline of the mid-back, in the dip under the 9th chest-level spine bump, about two bumps below the level of the lower tips of the shoulder blades.
On the midline of the mid-back, in the dip under the 7th chest-level spine bump, level with the lower tips of the shoulder blades.
On the midline of the upper back, in the dip under the 6th chest-level spine bump, just above the lower tips of the shoulder blades.
On the midline of the upper back, in the dip under the 5th chest-level spine bump, between the shoulder blades.
On the midline of the upper back, in the dip under the 3rd chest-level spine bump, level with where the shoulder-blade ridge meets the spine.
On the midline of the upper back, in the dip under the first chest-level spine bump, just below the big bump at the base of the neck.
At the base of the neck on the midline, in the dip just under the biggest bump you feel when you tilt your head forward.

On the back of the neck, on the midline, about half a thumb-width above the hairline: in the hollow just above the first bony bump you feel at the top of the neck, below the base of the skull. Press lightly.
indications: headache at the back of the head

find: On the back of the head, on the midline just below the bony bump at the base of the skull, in the hollow between the two neck muscles.
On the midline at the back of the head, in the hollow just above the bony bump at the base of the skull.
On the midline at the back of the head, about two finger-widths above the hollow that sits just over the bony bump at the base of the skull.
On the midline at the back of the top of the head, about two finger-widths behind the very top of the head.
At the very top of the head on the midline, a little forward of halfway between the front and back hairlines; also where a line joining the tips of both folded-forward ears crosses the midline.
On the midline of the scalp, about two finger-widths (one and a half thumb-widths) in front of the crown point at the very top of the head.
On the midline of the scalp, about two thumb-widths behind the front hairline.
On the midline of the scalp, one thumb-width behind the front hairline.
On the midline of the scalp, half a thumb-width behind the front hairline.
On the very tip of the nose, at the centre of the rounded end.
On the midline of the upper lip, in the vertical groove under the nose, around its middle or a little nearer the nose.
note: WHO places this in the middle of the groove under the nose; many references use the spot one third of the way down. Either is fine.

find: On the midline of the upper lip, at the middle of the small bump in the centre of the lip edge.
Inside the mouth, where the small fold of skin joining the upper lip meets the upper gum, on the midline.
avoidReason: Inside the mouth under the lip; cannot be sensibly self-pressed.

find: In the soft area between the anus and the genitals, at the midpoint.
avoidReason: In the perineal region, not sensible or appropriate to self-press.

find: On the lower belly, on the midline, just above the top edge of the pubic bone.
On the lower belly, on the midline, about four thumb-widths below the navel.
On the lower belly, on the midline, about three thumb-widths (four finger-widths) below the navel.
On the lower belly, on the midline, about two thumb-widths below the navel.
On the lower belly, on the midline, about one and a half thumb-widths (two finger-widths) below the navel.
On the lower belly, on the midline, about one thumb-width below the navel.
In the centre of the navel, inside the belly button.
avoidReason: Lies inside the navel; not pressed directly.

find: On the upper belly, on the midline, about one thumb-width above the navel.
On the upper belly, on the midline, about two thumb-widths above the navel.
On the upper belly, on the midline, about three thumb-widths above the navel.

On the upper belly, on the midline, halfway between the navel and the point where the lower end of the breastbone meets the rib arch (not the loose tip below it), about four thumb-widths above the navel.
On the belly midline, about four finger-widths plus two thumb-widths above the navel, a little more than halfway from the navel up to the bottom of the breastbone.
On the belly midline, about two thumb-widths below where the ribs meet at the bottom of the breastbone (roughly four finger-widths plus three thumb-widths above the navel).
On the midline, one thumb-width below the spot where the flat breastbone ends and its small pointed tip begins. Press lightly.
On the midline of the chest, right at the bottom of the breastbone where it meets the soft upper belly. Use light pressure.
On the middle of the chest, on the breastbone, level with the space between the 4th and 5th ribs (count down from the collarbone). In many men this is nipple height.
On the middle of the breastbone, level with the space between the 3rd and 4th ribs, about two finger-widths above the 4th-rib level of the chest centre.
On the middle of the breastbone, level with the gap between the 2nd and 3rd ribs, a few finger-widths below the collarbone line.
On the upper part of the breastbone, in line with the first gap between ribs just below the collarbone, about a thumb-width below the next point up.
On the upper breastbone, about one thumb-width below the hollow at the base of the throat.
In the soft hollow at the base of the throat, just above the top of the breastbone, between the inner ends of the collarbones. Use very light pressure.
On the front midline of the neck, in the dip just above the bony hyoid ridge, between the chin and the Adam's apple. Use very light pressure.
On the chin, in the middle of the dip between the lower lip and the point of the chin. Press lightly.
On the upper back, just beside the spine at the base of the bony bump at the bottom of the neck, about half a thumb-width out to the side.
On the lower belly: one hand-width plus one thumb-width below the navel, then one hand-width (four finger-widths) out to the side.
On the top of the head, a set of four spots: one thumb-width in front of, behind, and to each side of the very top of the head.
indications: headache at the top of the head

find: Front of the thigh: find the spot three finger-widths above the outer top corner of the kneecap. The two points sit two finger-widths to the outside and two finger-widths to the inside of that spot.
On the back of the elbow, at the very tip of the pointed bone that sticks out when you bend your arm.
A row of points on each side of the spine, from the top of the upper back down to the low back, each about half a thumb-width out from the bony bumps of the spine.
On the front of the scalp, straight up from the pupil when you look ahead, one thumb-width back from the front hairline.
Just above the kneecap, in the small hollow at the middle of its upper edge.
Inner forearm, a hand-width plus a thumb-width above the wrist crease. Two spots, one on each side of the tendon on the thumb side (it pops up when you bend the wrist toward the thumb).
On the mid-back: find the spine bump level with the bottom tips of the shoulder blades, go one bump lower, then two finger-widths out to the side, level with the gap just below that bump.
On the forehead, in the flat spot exactly halfway between the inner ends of your eyebrows.
indications: headache at the front of the head

find: Inner front of the thigh: one hand-width (four finger-widths) straight up from the inner top corner of the kneecap, on the bulge of the inner thigh muscle.
On the back of the wrist, in the hollow along the wrist crease just on the thumb side of the main finger-straightening tendon.

On the low back: find the first bump of the low back (three bumps above the one level with the hip-bone tops), then go one hand-width plus half a thumb-width out to the side, level with the gap just below it.
On the eyebrow, at its middle, directly above the pupil when you look straight ahead. Stay on the brow bone.
indications: headache at the front of the head

find: With the knee bent, in the soft dip just below the kneecap on the inner side of the thick tendon.
On the back of the middle finger, at the centre of the middle joint (the knuckle halfway along the finger). Bend the finger slightly; it is at the top of the bent joint.
On the low back, in the middle line of the spine, just under the third bony bump of the low back.
In the soft hollow of the temple, about one thumb-width behind the middle of the line from the outer end of the eyebrow to the outer corner of the eye.
With the knee bent, in the two soft dips just below the kneecap, one on each side of the thick tendon. The inner dip is Neixiyan.
On the back of the thumb, in the middle of the crease at the thumb's only knuckle joint.
On the low back: find the spine bump level with the tops of the hip bones, then go one hand-width (four finger-widths) out to the side, level with the gap just below it.
At the very top of the ear. Fold the ear forward and it is at the tip of the fold.
Outer side of the lower leg: find the bony knob below the outer knee and the hollow just below and in front of it. Go three finger-widths further down from that hollow and press for the tender spot.
On the back of the little finger, at the centre of the middle joint (the knuckle halfway along the finger).
On the low back, in the dimple one hand-width plus half a thumb-width out from the spine, level with the gap below the spine bump that lines up with the tops of the hip bones.
On the lower rim of the eye socket, about one quarter of the way in from the outer corner of the eye.
avoidReason: Sits right under the eyeball and is needled deep by specialists; pressing here risks pushing into the eye.

find: Front of the lower leg: one hand-width plus three finger-widths below the bottom of the kneecap, one finger-width outside the shin bone. Press for the tender spot.
On the back of the hand, two points: one between the index and middle finger bones and one between the ring and little finger bones, about halfway from wrist to knuckles.
note: References differ on whether these sit midway between wrist and knuckles or nearer the wrist. This follows the midway version.

find: On the middle line of the low back, in the small hollow just below the last bony bump of the low back, where it meets the sacrum.
On the face, at the top end of the groove running from the side of the nostril, where the nose cartilage meets the bone.
On the inner side of the ankle, at the very top of the rounded bony bump.

english: Outer Palace of Toil / Stiff Neck Point
find: On the back of the hand, in the tender hollow between the index and middle finger bones, about half a thumb-width behind the knuckles.
On the middle line of the lower back, three finger-widths above the tip of the tailbone, in the hollow between the two small bony ridges at the lower end of the sacrum.
note: References differ on the height. This follows the version two thumb-widths above the tip of the tailbone.

find: Inside the nostril, high up, where the nose meets the upper lining.
avoidReason: Inside the nose; needled or pricked with an endoscope by practitioners and not something to press yourself.

find: On the outer side of the ankle, at the very top of the rounded bony bump.
On the back of the hand, in the four hollows between the knuckles of neighbouring fingers, just behind the finger webs. Four points on each hand.
In the mouth, on the middle of the tongue top when the tongue is stuck fully out.
avoidReason: On the tongue; not suitable for self-pressing.

find: On the top of the foot, in the four hollows between neighbouring toes, just behind the toe webs. Four points on each foot.
On the palm side of the index, middle, ring and little fingers, at the centre of the middle crease of each finger (the joint halfway along). Four points on each hand.
In the mouth, under the tongue, in the middle of the fold of skin holding the tongue down.
avoidReason: Under the tongue; traditionally pricked to bleed, not suitable for self-pressing.

find: On the underside of the second toe, in the middle of the crease at the joint nearest the toenail.
At the very tip of each of the ten fingers, just beyond the nail edge. Press with the edge of a fingernail on each tip.
In the mouth, under the left side of the tongue, on the vein beside the central fold of skin.
avoidReason: Under the tongue on a vein; traditionally pricked to bleed, not suitable for self-pressing.

find: At the tip of each of the ten toes, just beyond the nail edge. Press with the edge of a fingernail.
In the mouth, under the right side of the tongue, on the vein beside the central fold of skin.
avoidReason: Under the tongue on a vein; traditionally pricked to bleed, not suitable for self-pressing.

find: Behind the ear, on the back edge of the bony bump behind the ear, about one thumb-width behind the soft hollow below the earlobe.
On the back of the neck: find the hollow just below the big bump at the base of the neck, go two thumb-widths straight up, then one thumb-width out to the side.

Behind the ear: find the soft hollow just behind the earlobe and the hollow under the base of the skull at the side of the neck. The point is halfway between them, just behind the bony bump behind the ear. Press lightly.
On the ear, along the raised inner ridge (not the outer rim), in its upper part, roughly a third of the way down from the top.
